body:
Parent: #245. Sibling: #248 scales final changed runs **within one file**; #249 widens daemon concurrency. This issue scales the **number of changed files, directories and names in one Workspace generation**. Completing #248 alone does not make a package install/update involving hundreds or thousands of tiny files admissible.

## Current source and failure chain

Source pin: current Core `main` at `a72d07ef81794f1a7224eb721c8673e503cfcb33` (2026-09-26). The ordinary route is public `WorkspaceApi::exec` → POSIX operations on the FUSE mount → explicit `WorkspaceApi::commit`.

- `State::frontier_bytes` rejects more than **128 dirty identities** or **128 changed names** and ties admission to a **32 KiB inline metadata request** ([source](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/blob/a72d07ef81794f1a7224eb721c8673e503cfcb33/core/crates/layerfs-workspace/src/runtime/state.rs#L196)).
- A local directory record stores `count: u16`, rejects `count > 128`, and some binding/tombstone operations rebuild up to 128 names into a `Vec` ([source](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/blob/a72d07ef81794f1a7224eb721c8673e503cfcb33/core/crates/layerfs-workspace/src/overlay/directories.rs#L23)).
- Commit lowering materializes directory rows and checks 128 again; `PreparedChanges` owns `Vec`s of directories/inodes, Bridge refuses >128 entries/names and limits the metadata request to 32 KiB ([lowering](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/blob/a72d07ef81794f1a7224eb721c8673e503cfcb33/core/crates/layerfs-workspace/src/commit/directories.rs#L18), [contract](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/blob/a72d07ef81794f1a7224eb721c8673e503cfcb33/core/crates/layerfs-bridge/src/contract/request.rs#L586)).
- The live node table has a **256-entry** ceiling; active handle and directory-cookie ceilings and linear `fresh`/`declared`/node lookups need audit under a many-file workload ([source](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/blob/a72d07ef81794f1a7224eb721c8673e503cfcb33/core/crates/layerfs-workspace/src/runtime/state.rs#L14)). C1's current filesystem input also accepts materialized slices and collects touched serials; its ordering budget is real, but its input and peak memory must scale deliberately.
- A fixed page fanout or a **128-entry readdir page** may remain as a bounded batch size. It must not cap the total directory or generation.

Raising one constant moves the refusal downstream. A generation that updates 129 small files can fail even if each file has only one changed byte and #248 has removed the per-file run ceiling.

## Target architecture

```text
BEFORE                                      AFTER
POSIX creates/updates                      POSIX creates/updates
  -> 128 dirty/names admission               -> resource-charged, path-local namespace COW
  -> bounded per-directory name Vec           -> ordered bindings/tombstones; no whole-dir rebuild
  -> freeze G1                                -> freeze immutable G1; G2 remains writable
  -> materialized PreparedChanges Vec         -> bounded cursor over final G1 names/inodes
  -> 32 KiB inline HistoryCommand             -> streamed, validated prepared update
  -> C1 consumes one bounded batch            -> C1 consumes replayable ordered input/spool
  -> one Stage/Commit if admitted              -> one exact filesystem root and Branch head
```

The final namespace change set is derived from the frozen generation, not a log of every shell operation. Keep `expected_head`, authenticated base/root, serial allocation, link counts, deletion/tombstone semantics, old-head readability and known/unknown outcome custody. A successful Commit installs the saved root as the next generation's base; writes accepted during Commit remain in the successor and appear in its later Commit. No intermediate Branch head is published for a batch page.

## Concrete algorithm and bounds

Let `F` be final changed inode identities, `K` final changed directory names, `B` their encoded bytes, and `H` the private page-tree height.

1. **Maintain final live state, not an operation log.** The existing generation-keyed dirty-serial index already records one key per dirty identity, and ordinary create already uses a keyed `candidate.update` for one directory binding. Keep those. Add path-local delete/rebind for the binding and tombstone trees; the current `keep_name`, `drop_entry` and `remove_name` paths collect/rebuild the directory and cannot remain `O(K)` per tiny-file mutation. Each mutation checks actual quota, writes only the touched leaf/ancestors, and atomically swaps the local root. Store wide, checked counts/bytes in a versioned directory record; no 128 or `u16` total-name admission.
2. **Bound the observation cache by ownership, not by files changed.** Index live nodes by serial, reclaim unpinned entries, and charge genuinely pinned kernel lookups/handles to the memory budget. A 256-entry cache ceiling or a linear scan of every prior node cannot replace the dirty-identity ceiling. A bounded readdir page or simultaneous-handle slot remains a page/concurrency limit, never a total-directory limit.
3. **Freeze G1 and stream its final namespace.** Pin its immutable root at a short ordering point; G2 mutations use a new root. Walk G1's dirty serials in serial order and each changed directory's bindings/tombstones in name order with persistent page cursors. Reuse the submission's private saved-result tree for content/metadata roots. An optional first pass computes checked record/byte totals; a second pass emits the same immutable rows in fixed-size frames. Frame size (including 128 rows if convenient) is a transport batch, not a generation cap.
4. **Validate, replay and build once.** The service validates strict ordering, unique serials/names, declared totals, role/link rules and exact EndInput while spooling input under a disk quota. C1 reads replayable ordered cursors from that spool; its current slice inputs and touched-serial `Vec` must become bounded iteration or budgeted external merge where their size grows with `F + K`. Feed the canonical filesystem builder one final state and publish one Stage/Commit result, preserving the old root identity for previously accepted inputs. A 129-row operation must not be split into two Branch commits.

Target local namespace work is `O(H)` touched pages per name/identity mutation, plus its actual payload I/O. Frozen lowering visits `O(F + K)` final records with amortized `O(H + touched leaves)` page visits per ordered cursor; C1 may use bounded external merge passes when it needs a second ordering, but no repeated whole-directory or whole-frontier scan per record. Resident memory is bounded by fixed buffers, tree paths and quota-charged *active pins*; temporary disk is charged by actual final records/bytes and merge runs. Quota or deadline exhaustion remains a precise refusal. These bounds are targets to verify with page-visit, allocation, spool and I/O counters, not measured claims.

## Implementation work

1. **Live namespace:** remove cardinality admission from `frontier_bytes` while retaining checked real memory/disk/deadline budgets. Use the existing keyed private page arena for path-local binding and tombstone insertion/deletion, rather than rescanning/rebuilding a whole directory on each tiny-file operation. Widen or version the directory count/byte representation so 128 and `u16` do not become replacement ceilings. Preserve atomic local-root publication and read-your-writes.
2. **Live caches/accounting:** make ordinary sequential creates/opens/forgets work beyond the 256-node cache and audit `fresh`, `declared`, `unbound`, handles and cookies for hidden count ceilings or cumulative quadratic lookups. Evict only unpinned observations; live handles and kernel lookup references remain valid. Charge simultaneous open handles and directory cursors to actual memory/FD/private-backing budgets; no fixed 128-handle or 1,024-cookie admission may bind while those budgets have room. Keep total files changed independent of live-handle count.
3. **Frozen lowering and wire:** walk dirty serials and directory bindings in stable order with bounded cursors. Replace the 32 KiB inline `PreparedChanges` payload and 128-entry decoders with a checked, replayable streaming form; validate ordering, exact counts/bytes and final EndInput before publication. Use quota-charged temporary backing for input too large for the fixed resident window. Both explicit Stage and ordinary Commit must use the same final-state path.
4. **C1/C5:** build one canonical filesystem result from the prepared stream with bounded resident state and spill/merge where needed. Reuse untouched subtrees, retain one-worker construction, and publish one Stage/Commit outcome. Preserve the exact canonical root for inputs the old ≤128 path accepts. Count C1 touched-serial, mapping and ordering work; avoid a new small fixed record cap.
5. **Performance and consistency:** diagnose per-file SaveFile/metadata round trips, private page operations and namespace lookup costs through the public route. Optimize any measured per-file overhead required for a many-tiny-file Exec and Commit to meet the repository performance gates. #249 removes the whole-Exec product runtime deadline; per-syscall and Commit deadlines remain. Prove G1/G2 reconciliation with hundreds of identities; do not enlarge budgets to pass.

## Acceptance

- Public SDK-only workload: one `WorkspaceApi::exec` runs an ordinary file producer through FUSE to create/update **129 names in one directory**, then a separate case changes **257 files** across directories, and a load-bearing package-tree case changes **1,025 tiny files/names** in one generation. Use closed prepared masters and independent writable copies. Exact full-tree bytes, modes, paths, absences, old-head readback and cleanup are checked by an independent verifier. Record actual FUSE calls and per-phase wall; no direct Workspace/Bridge/C1 mutation calls in the benchmark driver.
- Focused tests cover the next count boundary beyond `u16`, mixed create/rename/delete/recreate/hardlink, pagination across more than 1,024 entries on one live directory handle, one directory with many local bindings and tombstones, more than 128 simultaneous active handles when resources permit, and simultaneous active handles versus total changed files. Genuine quota/disk/deadline exhaustion returns a precise failure without partial Branch publication.
- Two sequential Commits prove the second uses the first saved filesystem root and includes only second-generation namespace changes. A mounted write accepted during G1's Commit is visible in G2 and saved by the next Commit.
- Demonstrate path-local live updates (target `O(log M)` touched namespace pages per mutation) and bounded ordered Commit traversal, with resident memory determined by declared buffers/tree height rather than total changed identities. Report actual spool high-water, page visits, lookup work, C1 ordering work, private disk and file-backed cache. Record Exec wall under the repository complete-command/cache rules; one registered sample per case/arm, no benchmark timeout/worker/quota inflation. #249 removes the fixed whole-Exec product runtime maximum.

Implementation can progress alongside #248. Its final many-file performance admission should use #248's improved write path. #245 cannot claim package-install/update scale until both file-run and namespace-cardinality gates pass.

## Load-bearing namespace review — 2026-09-26

The [post-#252 case review](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/blob/codex/issue245-joint-tree-research/core/docs/issues/245/LOAD_BEARING_CASE_REVIEW.md) found a further namespace count gate: C1's `MAXIMUM_WALK_ENTRIES=4,096` reachability/cycle validation can refuse a wide base-directory rebind before configured resources are exhausted ([source](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/blob/f74dbe77da12fa533587be8a578375bce3f19373/core/crates/layerfs-content/src/filesystem/limits.rs#L86)). #256 must replace this fixed visited-binding admission with resource-charged checked traversal and prove a public wide-base-tree operation across that boundary. Removing the Workspace 128-name checks alone does not qualify the many-package/remove-and-copy cases.

A **base-resident directory move** is a separate semantic gap, tracked in sibling [#258](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/issues/258): current `moved_identity` returns `Unsupported` because inherited descendants resolve by old canonical paths. A fresh-upper directory move is not proof for that case. Keep #256's count/streaming proof and #258's origin/identity proof distinct.

comments.body:
The current-source namespace-tree capacity and complexity review for #256 is in draft PR #257: https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/pull/257

At f74dbe77, the keyed private index already supports path-copied inserts. The report sizes 129/257/1,025/65,536 empty-file shapes and the separate in-flight saved-result tree, then traces the count refusals through directory delete/rebuild, 256 active nodes, reconciliation's 64-page/26-slot reserve, 32 KiB/u16 prepared input, and C1's 4,096-pending spill without FileBacking. It proposes path-local delete, retained cursors, progressive multilevel building and one streamed/validated prepared update with a single Branch-head publication. The estimates are algebraic, not a benchmark or admission PASS.

## Shared phase-1 ownership substrate landed (the #248/#256 common slice)

The post-Phase-1 sequence implements one shared private page/payload ownership
substrate for #248 and #256 before either issue's own tree work. That slice is
implemented and measured on branch `codex/issue245-post-phase1-implementation`
(base `origin/main` `f74dbe77d`):

- `b298d175d` instrument(core): count routine private-ownership work
- `7e6cac877` perf(core): index the ownership registry and drive reclamation by work

Full detail, receipts and limits are on
[#248](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/issues/248#issuecomment-5844790127);
this comment records what it means for #256.

Relevant to this issue: the private ownership registry is now indexed by payload
id and routine maintenance is work-driven, so a namespace mutation that admits
one small private payload no longer pays work proportional to every earlier
acquisition. `BackingStatus` gains two saturating work counts
(`routine_scans`, `lookup_scans`) that this issue's live-cache and
frozen-lowering work can use the same way — an operator-visible count of private
work per accepted mutation, not a timer. Quota refusal is precise
(`Backing { phase: Acquire, kind: StorageFull }`), charges nothing, drops
nothing, and keeps every existing owner accounted and readable.

Nothing in #256's own scope is done or claimed by this commit: the 128
dirty-identity/name and 32 KiB prepared-metadata admissions, path-local
delete/rebind, the prepared-stream wire form, C1 ordering and the
`MAXIMUM_WALK_ENTRIES = 4,096` reachability admission are all still open, and
the 129/257/1,025 changed-file gates have not been attempted. The next phase in
the sequence is #248's file/Commit path; #256's keyed namespace and prepared
stream follow it, implemented on this same substrate.

Receipts: `core/docs/issues/245/evidence/post-phase1-ownership-v1/`.

**Phase-3 lane opened: the first refusal is pinned, no product change yet.**

Commit `c30fe68a0` on `codex/issue245-post-phase1-implementation` adds one external case and no product change. It creates 200 names in one directory through the public API, then renames 60, unlinks 60 and recreates 25, checking the exact listing at each stage.

Observed refusal at head, through the ordinary mounted route:

```
create 127: Capacity
WorkspaceStatus { generation: 1, revision: 127, dirty_inodes: 128, nodes: 128,
                  accounted_bytes: 1999264, active_operations: 0 }
```

It comes from `State::frontier_bytes` in `runtime/state.rs`, which refuses `dirty > 128 || names > 128` and then bounds the prepared-namespace size it computes by `layerfs_bridge::contract::METADATA_BYTES` (32 KiB). So the first admission this issue owns is not the directory page at all: it is the generation frontier, and both of its bounds are aggregate admissions rather than charged resources.

Reproduce on demand (the case is `#[ignore]`d with that reason so the suite stays green):

```
TMPDIR=/src/tmp cargo test --release --locked --manifest-path core/Cargo.toml \
  -p layerfs-workspace --test wide_namespace -- --ignored --nocapture
```

Where the caps sit, from the source, in the order this issue has to lift them:

| Layer | Bound |
| --- | --- |
| `runtime/state.rs` `frontier_bytes` | `dirty > 128`, `names > 128`, computed prepared size `> METADATA_BYTES` (32 KiB) |
| `overlay/directories.rs` | `Directory::parse` refuses `count > 128`; `keep_name`/`drop_entry`/`remove_name` rebuild a whole page from a resident `Vec` of at most 128 names |
| `overlay/snapshot.rs` | 32,768-byte prepared-metadata charge |
| `commit/directories.rs` | `vector(128 + …)` and `rows.len() == 128` / `changes.len() == 128` |
| `commit/reconcile.rs` | `state.dirty_inodes > 128` |
| `bridge/contract/request.rs` | `directories.len() > 128 \|\| inodes.len() > 128`, `count > 128`, `METADATA_BYTES = 32768` |

The keyed index has no point delete at all today (`Arena::update` inserts; `next` is a fresh root-to-leaf descent per call), which is why directory mutation rebuilds whole pages and why a name walk is `O(H)` per name. Path-local delete plus a persistent ordered key cursor is the substrate this issue needs before any of the counts above can be lifted honestly.

**Phase 3 slices 3.0-3.2 landed on the #245 implementation lane. `wide_namespace.rs` passes.**

Commits on `codex/issue245-post-phase1-implementation`:

- `bd907b5ba` - slice 3.0, relocation only: the two private tree algorithms now live in `backing/binary_plus_tree/{extent,keyed}/`, with every old module path kept as a reexport. The whole existing `layerfs-workspace` suite ran unedited, 52/0/137, identical to the parent run from an extracted pristine tree. Migration, not an algorithm change: +37 production lines of module docs, reexport blocks and rewritten `use` lists.
- `8460f5afc` - slices 3.1 and 3.2.

**3.1 path-local namespace mutation.** `keyed/delete.rs` adds `RootOwner::delete` (one key out of one leaf, copied along its own path; a page the removal empties leaves its parent; a page it leaves under the minimum body is merged or split with one neighbour at its own level; a root that keeps one child is lifted out). `keyed/cursor.rs` adds `Arena::key_cursor`, a persistent ordered walk that keeps its path across leaves, `O(H + L)` page reads. `keep_name`/`drop_entry`/`remove_name` are point mutations on those, not a whole-page walk into a resident `Vec` of at most 128 names plus a rebuild. `Directory::parse` and the rename path no longer refuse a directory that binds more than 128 names; the `u16` count and byte field are unchanged and still charged per name.

**3.2 the frontier is charged, not counted.** `State::frontier_bytes` still computes the exact prepared-namespace bytes, but no longer refuses `dirty > 128 || names > 128` and no longer compares the total against `METADATA_BYTES` (32 KiB). It reserves that total from the host's own declared memory budget and follows the frontier, one reservation at a time, released when the capture resets the counters. A refusal is now the configured budget refusing.

`core/docs/architecture/06-limits.md` records the keyed tree's declared bounds and the removal invariants in the same commit.

**Checks** (locked release, Linux ext4 container): `wide_namespace` 2 passed / 7.3 s - the pinned case now reads `WIDE_NAMESPACE names=165 dirty_inodes=166 revision=345` where `c30fe68a0` refused `create 127: Capacity`; one unlink of a 130-name directory reads 40 metadata pages (`UNLINK_PATH`, bound 48, the rebuild it replaces is above a hundred); `keyed_tree` 1 passed / 0.22 s with `KEYED_WALK keys=160 leaves=2 reads=3` and `KEYED_DELETE deleted=160 candidates=8`; whole package 55 passed / 0 failed / 136 ignored against 53/0/136 at the parent; clippy no error; fmt clean; product-boundary guard PASS (306 files), self-tests 7 passed. Production LOC 56178 -> 56414 (delta +236).

**Limits.** One deletion shape is refused as `Capacity` rather than published: a pair of pages whose cells total more than one page's 128 cells while their bytes are fewer than two pages' minimum, which no legal pair of pages can hold - the page format is unchanged. `wide_namespace.rs` also needed three fixture corrections to reach the refusal it pinned (no `Inspect::List` answer for the attached root; a `readdir` helper that counted entries instead of resuming at the returned cookie; an oracle that kept the rename sources and dropped the recreated names). The workload and its assertions are unchanged.

**Still open for this issue:** slice 3.3 (`commit/directories.rs` still holds `vector(usize::from(directory.count) + 128)`, `rows.len() == 128`, `changes.len() == 128`, and a successor lookup per name) and slice 3.4 (the prepared namespace is still resident through Bridge/server/C1). Phase 3 is not closed.

**Slice 3.2's second half: the live-node table is charged, not capped at 256.** Commit `0d974fa82`.

With the frontier charged, the next aggregate admission a wide generation met was `NODE_LIMIT = 256`: a 64 MiB budget admitted 255 creations and refused the 256th (`nodes: 256`). `State::reserve_nodes` now grows the table by charged `NODE_LIMIT` chunks against the host's own declared memory budget; the attach floor is unchanged (the first chunk is charged where the node table was charged before, under its own charge), and `check_child_stamp`/`cache_lookup` grow instead of testing the length.

Measured: `a_spent_budget_refuses_precisely_and_publishes_nothing` selects 4 MiB and creates until refusal - `FRONTIER_REFUSED index=511 revision=511 listed=511`, two chunks past 256, `Capacity`, revision and listing unmoved, the would-be name absent, the same name refused again. The 1,025-identity shape is `a_generation_admits_many_identities_while_its_budget_has_room`: **all 1,025 creations are admitted** at 64 MiB; the complete listing then refuses at the fixed 1,024-entry cookie table (`listed=1_022`, `Capacity`) - not at the frontier. The case is `#[ignore]`d with its measured wall (44.7 s, one command over the 30 s rule) as the reason, so it is a pin run on demand rather than a gate. Whole package 56 passed / 0 failed / 137 ignored; clippy no error; fmt clean; boundary guard PASS (306 files) + 7 self-tests. Production LOC 56414 -> 56437.

**Next refusals this lane measured, in order, for the remaining work** - none of them fixed here:

1. `runtime::state::COOKIE_LIMIT = 1024` - a complete listing of a generation wider than 1,022 names.
2. `commit/save.rs` still refuses a prepared namespace whose computed size exceeds `layerfs_bridge::contract::METADATA_BYTES` (32 KiB) *at Commit*, so a wide generation admitted pre-Commit would be refused downstream. That check is slice 3.3's to charge.
3. `commit/directories.rs` still holds `vector(usize::from(directory.count) + 128)`, `rows.len() == 128`, `changes.len() == 128`, and one successor lookup per name - slice 3.3.
4. The prepared namespace is still resident through Bridge/server/C1 - slice 3.4.
5. `layerfs-content`'s 4,096-binding validation walk, to check before claiming a wide rebind passes.

Phase 3 is not closed: slices 3.3 and 3.4 remain.

**Correction to my previous comment on this issue.** The two figures I gave for the 1,025-identity pin were predictions from the counting code, not measurements: the case is `#[ignore]`d, and I had not run the rewrite. I have now run it on the committed source, and one of my numbers was wrong.

- **Wrong:** the generation's dirty count. It holds one dirty identity per created file **plus the directory they were created in**, so `dirty_inodes=1026`, not the 1,025 my comment implied. The assertion is fixed in `91b7f2b3`-equivalent commit `test(core): measure the 1,025-identity pin instead of predicting it (#256)`.
- **Right, now measured:** `FRONTIER_ADMITTED names=1025 dirty_inodes=1026 revision=1025` — all 1,025 creations admitted at a 64 MiB budget — and `FRONTIER_LISTING listed=1022 refusal=Some(Capacity)`, i.e. the complete listing stops at the fixed 1,024-entry cookie table after 1,022 names. Wall 44.73 s, which is the reason the case stays `#[ignore]`d rather than gating.

Nothing else in the previous comment changes: the frontier and live-node-table lifts, the `keyed_tree` counts, the 130-name unlink count and the package result are all measured. The lesson is recorded in the commit: a `#[ignore]`d pin still has to be run once before its numbers are quoted.

**Handoff updated for the next agent: slices 3.3 and 3.4 are one assignment.**

The coordination document `core/docs/issues/245/HANDOFF_POST_PHASE1_ITERATIVE_IMPLEMENTATION.md` (research PR #257) now carries the lane state at `861784ab7`, the phase-3 rows for 3.0-3.2 marked done with their commits, and a new section that fixes how the last two slices land:

- **Why 3.3 and 3.4 land together.** `commit/save.rs` still refuses a prepared namespace over `METADATA_BYTES` (32 KiB) at Commit. That check is the same figure 3.2 removed from the pre-Commit frontier, and removing it without 3.4's ordered replayable stream converts a refusal into an unbounded resident prepared namespace. So 3.3 either charges the prepared size precisely against the same host budget, or the spool of 3.4 lands with it.
- **The refusals a wide generation meets next**, each marked measured or open: the Commit-side 32 KiB check; `vector(usize::from(directory.count) + 128)`, `rows.len() == 128` and `changes.len() == 128` plus one successor lookup per name in `commit/directories.rs`; the resident prepared namespace through Bridge, the server and C1; the measured 1,024-entry cookie table; and `layerfs-content`'s 4,096-binding validation walk.
- **Where 3.3's focused test goes, and why.** `tests/commit_progress.rs` cannot exercise `prepared_directories`: its delivery deliberately refuses the file save, and `prepare_changes` runs after `persist_saved` in `commit/save.rs`, so the lowering never executes there. The usable harness is `tests/support/native_workspace.rs` - the gate-based fake Workspace and store that `tests/commit_staged.rs` drives - with the recorded `StageChanges` request as the oracle for "exact rows for a wide directory".
- **What not to rebuild.** The counts the lane already proves are listed with the commands to reuse (`wide_namespace` 3 cases in 14.0 s, `keyed_tree` in 0.22 s), and the environment recipe names the container, its target directory, and the two measured pitfalls: the container's own architecture, and a `TMPDIR` outside the ext2/3 volume failing the payload acquire with `Unsupported`.

No product source changed in that commit (`450445be4`, documentation only, production LOC delta 0).

**Slice 3.3 landed, and the admission half of 3.4 with it** — `e5c14c72c` on `codex/issue245-post-phase1-implementation` (parent `861784ab7`).

What the code does now:

- **The frozen namespace is lowered in one ordered pass per record kind.** `commit/lower.rs` walks the captured frontier with three persistent cursors over the one keyed tree (dirty records, namespace records, inode records) advanced together in serial order, and `prepared_inodes` reads the result records through a fourth cursor over the submission's result root. `commit/directories.rs` lowers a maintained directory by merging its entry leaves and its removal leaves in name order; `vector(128 + …)`, `rows.len() == 128` and `changes.len() == 128` are gone, and a removal row is reserved against the charge its tombstone already made. The walk holds **no metadata writer gate** (the frozen root is immutable and pinned, and a window is leased per step), which is 2.R2's scope decision: the "no Commit phase holds the writer gate across a frozen walk" sentence covers this walk, so the holds were narrowed here.
- **Admission is the exact encoded size, not a count.** `PreparedChanges::frame_bytes` is the whole request body the encoder writes; the workspace compares it against `METADATA_BYTES` and the contract compares it again at admission, so a caller other than the Workspace is bounded the same way. The 128-directory / 128-inode / 128-name caps in `bridge/contract/request.rs` are gone, and every decoded count is bounded by the bytes the frame still holds instead of a fixed maximum.

Evidence (locked release, Linux ext4 container `layerfs-i245-phase1`):

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `layerfs-workspace/tests/prepared_namespace.rs` (new, 3 cases) | 3 passed, 7.51 s |
| one 200-name Commit, 145 later name changes | `PREPARED_NAMESPACE names=165 rows=260 inodes=165 frame_bytes=17501 metadata_reads=1464 saves=165 metadata=165` |
| 200 links to one published identity | `PREPARED_NAME_PASS names=200 inodes=1 metadata_reads=21` |
| frame boundary, measured | `PREPARED_FRAME_FIT names=94 declared=32760 limit=32768`; `PREPARED_FRAME_REFUSAL names=95 declared=33106 limit=32768 error=Capacity` |
| `layerfs-bridge` package | 19 passed in `history_protocol`, all targets green, 13 s |
| `layerfs-workspace` package | 0 failed; `wide_namespace` 3 passed / 1 ignored / 13.78 s, `pieces_sequence` 33 passed / 0.17 s, `commit_progress` 1 passed / 16.22 s, `keyed_tree` 1 passed / 0.21 s |
| `layerfs-server` package | 0 failed, `history.rs` 28 passed, 13 s |
| clippy / fmt / boundary guard | no error or warning in changed files; `fmt --check` clean; boundary PASS (306 files), self-tests 7 passed |

The recorded request is asserted row by row: every bound name carries the serial the mounted creation returned, every rename source and removed name is stated absent, inode rows and fresh declarations are ordered and exact, and the same names are listed after reconciliation.

Still open in this issue:

- **3.4's stream.** The prepared rows are still resident through Bridge, the server and C1 — charged by `State::frontier_bytes` before Commit, not unbounded, but not a spool. A generation is therefore bounded by one metadata frame (about 338 five-byte names) rather than by the configured budget. The SaveFile/`FileInput` seam remains the model: validate the stream once into a bounded spool and feed C1's ordered builder from it.
- **The 1,024 cookie table** still stops a complete listing at 1,022 names.

### Slice 3.4, part 1 landed: C1 reads a prepared update as ordered rows

`7a81213ba` on `codex/issue245-post-phase1-implementation` (parent `b4a306bf2`).

**What changed.** The half the handoff named as the deep one: `FilesystemInput`
took `&[DirectoryUpdate]`, `&[InodeUpdate]` and `&[u64]` and answered
`update_for`/`value_for`/`new_inodes.contains` by binary search over those
resident vectors, so no spool could feed it however the rows arrived.

- `layerfs-content/src/filesystem/rows/` is the new input seam: `RowSource`
  (three ordered, replayable cursors plus `directory_for`/`value_for`/
  `new_position`), `PreparedRows` (those rows plus the fixed fields),
  `FilesystemInput` as the resident implementation, `PreparedUpdate` as the
  streamed pair, and `check_input`, which now also refuses a source whose
  cursors end anywhere but its declared totals.
- `validate.rs`/`update.rs` read the input through cursors; the directory
  phase holds one declared batch of rows and validation decodes one row at a
  time. The resident cost of reading a prepared namespace follows one row per
  pass, not the row count.
- `rows/spool.rs`: the file-backed row spool the server will feed. One fixed
  32-byte slot per row in key order (key, payload offset, length, binding
  count, kind) with payloads behind them; the slot table is sized from the
  declared totals at creation, a lookup is a binary search over a kind's slot
  run read from the file, a pass is one sequential walk of it. Every slot and
  payload is charged against a declared capacity before it is written, a key
  that does not rise inside its run is refused where it is written, `seal`
  refuses a spool that does not hold what it declared, and the file is removed
  on cleanup or drop.

### Slice 3.4 landed: the prepared namespace travels as a declared stream

`fb10e9b09` on `codex/issue245-post-phase1-implementation` (parent `7a81213ba`).
Phase 3's last slice is in, so **phase 3's five slices are all on the lane**.

**What changed.** The 32 KiB metadata frame is no longer a generation's bound.

- The request carries a *declaration*: the update's identity, the fields it is
  addressed with, and `PreparedTotals` - the exact directory rows, binding rows,
  naming bytes, identity rows, patches, declarations and fresh serials of the
  body that follows. `stream_bytes()` is the whole body from those counts, and
  that is what the transport streams and what `MAX_PREPARED_STREAM_BYTES`
  charges.
- The rows are one ordered body: a role per identity row (an existing or fresh
  file/symlink with its saved roots, a maintained directory's patch, or a fresh
  directory's declaration), in serial order, so the three lists the service used
  to merge are one pass.
- The Workspace **measures** the declaration by lowering the frozen frontier
  once without encoding, then lowers it again to write the body; the emit pass
  refuses to finish if its own counts differ from the declaration it was sent
  with. Memory follows the widest row, not the row count.
- The service receives the body into a charged `RowSpool`, giving each row its
  canonical work on the way in (role check, portable patch, first metadata),
  checks the base precondition in waves over the spool, and hands C1 a
  `PreparedUpdate` it reads through `RowSource`. The spool is removed when the
  update is done.

**Limits, stated rather than implied.** A receiver must read the body to know
what an update says, so a request that declares rows and never sends them fails
in the stream rather than at admission. The service's per-row role check and
metadata patching now happen inside the save, so an invalid update opens and
aborts a C2 save instead of being refused before one (nothing is published

the 200-name pass reads 32 metadata pages where the resident lowering read 21 -
which is the price of a measured declaration. A fixture delivery that does not
read the body never runs the emit pass; the in-process Commit fixture reads it,
and the native route always does.
